status: research rubric baseline; not a benchmark result
purpose: Define the contextual evidence layers required to assess local Hebrew-to-English Psalms translation at a scholarly level.

readiness_scale.1: Concept acknowledged, but evidence is manual, missing, or not integrated.
readiness_scale.2: Some source data exists, but retrieval or scoring is incomplete.
readiness_scale.3: Usable evidence exists for limited benchmark use, with known gaps.
readiness_scale.4: Strong current evidence and repeatable checks exist.
readiness_scale.5: Release-grade evidence, scoring, and review workflow exist.

context_layers.label: Canonical Hebrew control
current_evidence: Psalm source units exist in content/psalms.
Each unit has token IDs, source Hebrew, transliteration, and draft status.
required_next_evidence: Schema gate requiring every generated claim to cite unit_id and token_id.
Per-layer alignment coverage scoring.
evaluation_questions: Does the model preserve the source token inventory before paraphrase?
Does the output distinguish grammar from interpretation?
failure_modes: Theological conclusion presented as lexical fact.

context_layers.label: Morphology and lexeme control
current_evidence: OSHB-derived lemma, Strong number, morphology, readable morphology, and part-of-speech fields are present for most tokens.
The current corpus profile quantifies missing stem, lemma, and Strong coverage.
required_next_evidence: Stem normalization audit.
Reviewer rubric for unsupported morphology claims.
evaluation_questions: Does the model render person, number, gender, stem, suffixes, and construct chains correctly?
Does it flag weak or missing morphology evidence?
failure_modes: Inferring stem or semantic role where the source packet is missing it.
Flattening pronominal suffixes or construct chains into generic English.

context_layers.label: Psalms-internal lexical context
current_evidence: Current corpus_occurrence_refs are Psalm-only in the scanned content.
required_next_evidence: Lemma-sense clustering inside Psalms.
Prompt-visible concordance packet with ranked Psalm parallels.
evaluation_questions: Does the model use Psalm-local recurrence without forcing the same gloss everywhere?
Does it distinguish repetition, refrain, and formula from accidental lexical recurrence?
failure_modes: Treating a Psalm-local occurrence list as whole-Tanakh evidence.
Over-normalizing repeated words into one English gloss.

context_layers.label: Whole-Tanakh lexical and motif context
current_evidence: The raw UXLC zip contains canonical Tanakh book XML files.
The generated content packets are currently Psalms-only.
required_next_evidence: Build a derived whole-Tanakh lexical index from UXLC without mutating data/raw.
Add cross-book lemma and phrase retrieval to evidence packets.
Track whether a cited context comes from Torah, Prophets, or Writings.
evaluation_questions: Does the rendering account for usage outside Psalms when a lemma or motif demands it?
Does it cite cross-book context without inventing references?
failure_modes: Using Psalms-only evidence while claiming whole-Bible support.

context_layers.label: Poetic form and genre
current_evidence: Seed units are tagged for lament, doxology, wisdom, royal psalm, repetition, and parallelism risks.
No full-corpus cola, strophe, acrostic, or genre annotation exists yet.
required_next_evidence: Add genre and poetic-form annotations for benchmark units.
Add scoring for lineation, parallelism, terseness, repetition, and source-image preservation.
evaluation_questions: Does the English preserve the pressure between poetic cola?
Does it respect genre movement, such as lament-to-trust?
failure_modes: Flattening parallelism into a prose summary.
Padding terse Hebrew into explanatory commentary.

context_layers.label: Ancient Israelite cultural setting
current_evidence: The research report identifies temple, royal, cultic, justice, enemy, land, and covenant context as required.
No structured local cultural-context source pack exists yet.
required_next_evidence: Create source-governed notes for royal, temple, wisdom, lament, war, exile, and pilgrimage contexts.
Require cultural claims to be tagged as source-context, comparative ANE context, or later reception.
evaluation_questions: Does the model preserve ancient social and cultic imagery before modernizing it?
Does it avoid turning cultural explanation into translation text?
failure_modes: Modern devotional paraphrase replacing ancient imagery.
Cultural claims without source or period tagging.

context_layers.label: Textual witnesses and version boundaries
current_evidence: Every current unit has witness records.
The corpus includes English witnesses and a Septuagint Greek witness role.
required_next_evidence: Separate witness evidence from canonical Hebrew basis in every prompt.
Add DSS, Targum, Syriac, and Vulgate only when license and version pinning are solved.
Score witness-boundary errors explicitly.
evaluation_questions: Does the model cite a witness as a witness rather than replacing the Hebrew source?
Does it flag variant-sensitive passages instead of silently choosing a tradition?
failure_modes: English witness style leakage into generated translation.
LXX or later witness treated as canonical Hebrew without disclosure.

context_layers.label: Jewish and Christian reception history
current_evidence: Seed units tag known reception-history cases.
No local, versioned reception corpus or source-note layer exists yet.
required_next_evidence: Create perspective-tagged notes for Jewish, Christian, academic-critical, and liturgical reception.
Require model outputs to separate translation, interpretation, and reception.
evaluation_questions: Does the model identify divergent reception without collapsing it into the translation?
Does it avoid privileging one tradition while pretending neutrality?
failure_modes: Christological or anti-Christological overreach in the translation layer.
Treating later reception as the original grammatical meaning.

context_layers.label: Review signoff and governance
current_evidence: Review policy and audit policy define reviewer roles and promotion gates.
No completed canonical English rendering corpus exists for Psalms yet.
required_next_evidence: Create blind-review benchmark workflows for lexical, Hebrew, alignment, lyric, theology, and release reviewers.
Publish model-card style release records for every local adapter.
evaluation_questions: Can the model proposal be accepted, rejected, or revised through audited human review?
Can a later reviewer reconstruct exactly what evidence the model saw?
failure_modes: Model output entering canonical content without review.
Benchmark results without prompt, model, quantization, source, and reviewer provenance.

case_studies.why: Royal sonship language requires separating grammar, royal ideology, later Jewish reception, and Christian reception.
minimum_model_behavior: Identify the unit as royal/enthronement language before later reception.
Tag reception-history claims separately from translation claims.

case_studies.why: A disputed phrase must be handled as lexical and textual ambiguity rather than as a settled theological proof.
minimum_model_behavior: Surface ambiguity and preserve the source-token basis.
Do not hide the disputed status in a smooth rendering.

case_studies.why: Human status language is canonically reused and may interact with divine-being terminology and later theological interpretation.
minimum_model_behavior: Keep anthropology and divine-being terminology distinct.
Cite canonical reuse as reception/context rather than immediate grammar.

case_studies.why: A lament line with major liturgical and Christian afterlife must be translated source-first.
minimum_model_behavior: Render the lament and divine address before reception claims.
Keep later liturgical use outside the translation string.

case_studies.why: A contested suffering-lament passage tests textual-witness boundaries and reception-history discipline.
minimum_model_behavior: Mark the passage as variant-sensitive.
Do not convert witness disagreement into a silent canonical choice.

case_studies.why: A familiar line tests whether the model resists inherited English phrasing and preserves pastoral source imagery.
minimum_model_behavior: Avoid unlicensed witness phrasing.
Explain divine-name and shepherd imagery policy separately.

case_studies.why: Heart and spirit language requires Hebrew anthropology before later doctrinal categories.
minimum_model_behavior: Preserve source anthropology terms before abstraction.
Flag theological interpretation as interpretation.

case_studies.why: A core divergent-reception royal psalm requires grammar, royal setting, and later theological use to remain separate.
minimum_model_behavior: Distinguish speaker, addressee, divine name, and royal title.
Separate Jewish, Christian, and academic-critical reception claims.

case_studies.why: Melchizedek and priesthood language needs Genesis, royal ideology, and reception-history controls.
minimum_model_behavior: Cite priesthood and kingship as context before theological use.
Preserve uncertainty where interpretive traditions diverge.

case_studies.why: A short universal-praise unit tests whether compact Hebrew can receive broader exilic and nations-context without padding.
minimum_model_behavior: Preserve imperative praise language.
Keep broad nations-context in rationale rather than over-expanding the line.

case_studies.why: Violent imprecation demands translation, trauma context, ethics, and reception to remain distinguishable.
minimum_model_behavior: Do not sanitize or intensify the violent rhetoric.
Tag ethical reception separately from the source translation.

context_packet_contract.description: Canonical Hebrew unit ID, source text, token IDs, morphology, and missing-evidence flags.
Psalm-local lemma and phrase parallels, marked explicitly as Psalm-local.
Whole-Tanakh lexical and motif context, with book/division labels and retrieval provenance.
Genre, cola, parallelism, acrostic, repetition, terseness, and lineation notes where known.
Royal, temple, cultic, wisdom, lament, exile, war, pilgrimage, and covenant context as source-tagged notes.
Version-pinned witness data separated from the canonical Hebrew basis.
Perspective-tagged Jewish, Christian, academic-critical, and liturgical reception notes.
Reviewer roles, required approvals, known risks, and model-output gates.
